correctness.rationale: At depth t+max(a_i)+1 the present and absent all-marker subwords force the comparison word to contain exactly t ones and fix every zero gap, regardless of its presumed length or endpoint type. For the lower bound, a prefix ending with the i-th one is i-universal because it contains (01)^i, and appending zero first introduces 1^i0 at length i+1. The reverse suffix gives the corresponding t−i bound. The published repeated-letter and insertion identities therefore give sum of side distances t+a_i at a split of the i-th gap, including i=0 and t. The count follows by coefficient extraction from the positive bounded-composition polynomial; division by binom(n−t−1,t) and a fixed-t limit gives the simplex maximum law. Integrating the limiting tail yields the stated harmonic moments. An independent bounded replay checks 566 exact longest-gap insertion witnesses and 63 composition coefficients.
residual_risks: The replay checks small words and counts; the all-length and fixed-t limit claims use the proof rather than extrapolating.

evidence: Lemma 5.4 removes two neighboring isolated unlike letters and adds one to rho relative to the shortened word. broader_coverage.reasoning: These exact identities cover all boundary cases of the stated family, not just the subfamily with gaps at least two. The next check gives the direct specialization.

evidence: If a zero gap has length one, remove that zero and an immediately adjacent marker using Lemma 5.4; all other gaps survive unchanged and rho drops by one. Retain one gap if all have size one. Once only gaps of size ≥2 remain, process each remaining marker by Lemma 5.5, left to right. Each zero-descended run lengthens once for each original adjacent remaining marker, so the transformed endpoints have lengths a+1 and the interiors a+2; alphabet flips change no length. Lemma 5.3 gives rho=t_remaining+max(a_i), and pair-removal charges exactly restore t. When one gap remains, rho equals its unary length directly.
The budget h≤H now coincides with bounding every positive part by H−t−1, whose polynomial and fixed-k simplex limit require only ordinary inclusion–exclusion.
